name: Los Cerritos Ranch House

dates.altered: The site's own collection notes record a 1930s remodel of the adobe (contractors C.T. McGrew & Sons, architect Kenneth Wing, landscape designer Ralph D. Cornell) and an 1872 photograph in which the south wing still had its flat roof.

refs.title: Los Cerritos Ranch House - Wikipedia
refs.note: The land-grant article 'Rancho Los Cerritos' reads 'For the adobe, see Los Cerritos Ranch House', which is why the record is named for the house.

refs.note: Owner. 'The adobe house that serves as a National Historic Landmark was built by John Temple in 1844 as a headquarters for his large-scale cattle operation'; 'The flat roof is a feature of Spanish Colonial architecture while the two-story structure draws on the Monterey Colonial style'; an 1872 photograph in which 'the South Wing of the adobe still retains its flat roof'; a 1930s remodel by contractors C.T. McGrew & Sons, architect Kenneth Wing and landscape designer Ralph D. Cornell.

refs.title: Fun Facts about 1844 - Rancho Los Cerritos
refs.note: 'Massachusetts-born John Temple constructed the present two-story Monterey-style adobe here on-site in 1844 as headquarters for his large-scale cattle operation.'

note: Added 4 Sep 2026 as the Los Angeles-basin example, for a node whose geography lists 'Los Angeles and Santa Barbara' and whose exemplars were all north of Salinas. The owner's pages are the source for the building's form ('two-story Monterey-style adobe', flat-roofed wings). No HABS record was found: the search '"Los Cerritos" ranch house Long Beach HABS loc.gov pictures item' over loc.gov returned only a HAER record of the Henry Ford Bridge over Cerritos Channel. Nothing here states a dimension.
